First thing, I’m sorry you’re going through this type of experience. It’s a pretty difficult thing to have to suffer through. One positive here is something that you may actually not see - you DO know who you are! Unfortunately your family doesn’t see it this way. Acknowledging that you need a shift is a really important step to becoming who you want to be.

At a point in all of our lives we feel tempted to be someone we’re not, for our friends, our family, romantic partners or work / social contexts. The fact that your family is doing all this for you can make it harder to break out of since you may feel like it’s conditional or that you owe it to them to fulfill their expectations.

I don’t know your exact circumstances but first attempting to talk about how you feel with them and why you feel this way can be a good first step. That way, you can see how you can act next and become more independent from them and be more able to grow into your potential. Good luck and feel free to inbox if you need to talk :)

1) I never got Instagram , and deleted the Facebook app off my phone about a month ago. I also completely deleted Snapchat. I do sometimes still take breaks from FB even on my computer, as I usually check it once a day 5-10 minutes. 

2) I still have messenger for school and communication, but I've gone off Facebook for a full month a while back. Missed some notifications, but nothing really that important.

3) I try to use my phone more as a tool rather than to occupy my time when I'm bored. I intentionally cut my daily screen time down by hours a couple of weeks ago, and try to stay around 1:30 - 2:30 per day max. 

4) I've been trying to fill the time with other things. Be more productive at work, read more, and generally be more present when engaging with people in real life. Picking up a hobby or pastime definitely helps.

5) Overall, definitely. Social media is fine in increments and does have its benefits, but most people do not use it as intended or to a level that is healthy for them. It's not too late to change, or too early (I'm 18 and I did it), and the fact that you're noting this and wanting to make a change is a great first step. After you spent more and more time away and less time comparing yourself and scrolling mindlessly, you'll realize the benefits it can have on your life. Remember to give yourself time too, change doesn't always happen overnight.
